ai.literal: Giving, living so that fame arises, other than that, profit there is not for the soul.
ai.translation: To give to those in need and live a life of fame—besides this, there is no true gain for a living soul.
ai.modern: ஏழைகளுக்குக் கொடுப்பதும் புகழுடன் வாழ்வதும் ஆகிய அதைத் தவிர, மனித உயிர்க்கு வேறு எந்த இலாபமும் இல்லை.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the ultimate purpose of human existence. The poet asserts that giving to the needy (ītal) and living in a way that earns lasting fame (icaipaṭa vāḻtal) are the only true achievements. Any other material accumulation or success is not considered a real profit (ūtiyam) for the soul. The word 'icai' specifically denotes fame, emphasizing that a life remembered for its generosity is the only life of true value.

ai.literal: Those who speak, all that they speak, is the fame that stands upon those who give something to those who beg.
ai.translation: Of all the words spoken by those who speak, the only praise that endures is the fame of those who give to the needy.
ai.modern: புகழ்ந்து பேசுபவர்கள் பேசும் புகழுரைகள் எல்லாம், இரப்பவர்க்கு ஏதேனும் ஒன்றை வாரி வழங்குபவர்களின் மேல் நிலைத்து நிற்கும் புகழே ஆகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the ultimate source of lasting fame. The poet states that among all the topics and praises spoken by people, the only true praise that endures is the fame of those who give generously. The word 'ஈவார்' refers to those who give, and 'இரப்பார்' refers to those who ask or beg. The fame ('புகழ்') of such givers stands ('நிற்கும்') above all other subjects of human speech, making charity the highest virtue worthy of praise.

ai.literal: Other than the exalted fame that is peerless in the world, there is not one thing that stands without perishing.
ai.translation: Except for the exalted, peerless fame earned in this world, there is nothing else that remains imperishable.
ai.modern: ஒப்பற்ற இவ்வுலகத்தில் உயர்ந்த புகழைத் தவிர, அழியாமல் நிலைத்து நிற்கக்கூடிய வேறு ஒன்றும் இல்லை.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the eternal nature of true fame. In this transient world, everything eventually decays and perishes. The only exception is 'புகழ்' (fame) arising from noble deeds, described here as 'ஒன்றா' (peerless or unequaled). This exalted fame is the sole entity that stands 'பொன்றாது' (undying), outlasting the physical existence of the individual.

words.gloss: within the limits of the earth

ai.literal: If one achieves enduring fame within the limits of the earth, the world of the gods, without praising the wise sages, will praise them.
ai.translation: If a person achieves enduring fame within the boundaries of this earth, the world of the gods will cease to praise its own wise sages and will instead praise that famous person.
ai.modern: ஒருவர் இந்த நிலவுலகின் எல்லைக்குள் அழியாத புகழைச் செய்வாரானால், தேவர் உலகம் அங்குள்ள அறிஞர்களைப் போற்றாமல், இவரையே போற்றிப் புகழும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the supreme value of earning lasting fame in the mortal world. It states that if someone achieves enduring fame on earth, even the celestial world of the gods will ignore its own resident sages and wise beings to praise and welcome this extraordinary human. The word 'புலவர்' here refers to the wise or divine scholars of the heavenly realm, and 'புத்தேள் உலகு' refers to the world of the gods. The poet uses this comparison to show that true earthly fame transcends even the glory of the heavens.

ai.literal: Ruin that is like prosperity, and death that becomes continued existence, are rare for any except the eminent.
ai.translation: A ruin that yields prosperity and a death that becomes eternal living are impossible for any but the truly eminent.
ai.modern: புகழைத் தரும் வறுமையும், என்றும் நிலைத்திருக்கும் தன்மையுடைய சாவும் அறிவுடைய மேலோர்க்கு அல்லாமல் மற்றவர்களுக்குக் கிடைப்பது அரிது.
ai.explanation: The couplet explains how the eminent or wise (vittakar) transcend the physical limitations of loss and death through their fame. A loss or ruin (kēṭu) suffered by them in the path of virtue is actually like prosperity (nattam) because it enhances their glory. Similarly, their physical death (cākkāṭu) is not an end but becomes a form of eternal existence (uḷatākum) because their fame lives on forever. Such noble transformations of adversity and mortality are impossible for ordinary people and belong only to the truly accomplished.

ai.literal: If appearing, with fame let one appear; than appearing, for those who do not have that, not appearing is better.
ai.translation: If you are to appear in the world, appear with fame; for those who lack it, it is better not to appear at all than to live without renown.
ai.modern: ஒருவர் உலகில் தோன்றுவதானால் புகழுடன் தோன்ற வேண்டும்; அத்தகைய புகழ் இல்லாதவர்கள் உலகில் தோன்றுவதை விடத் தோன்றாமல் இருப்பதே நல்லது.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the supreme value of a life of fame and honor. The word 'தோன்றின்' (if one appears) refers to entering public life or being born into the world. The author states that if a person is to make an appearance in society, they should do so with the distinction of fame ('புகழொடு தோன்றுக'). For those who do not possess such fame ('அஃதிலார்'), the act of appearing or living in the public eye ('தோன்றலின்') is far less desirable than not appearing or not being born at all ('தோன்றாமை நன்று'). This stark contrast highlights that a life without honor or contribution is equivalent to non-existence.

ai.literal: Those who do not live so that fame arises do not blame themselves; what is the use of blaming those who despise them?
ai.translation: What is the point of blaming those who despise them, when those who fail to live a life of fame do not blame themselves?
ai.modern: புகழ் உண்டாகும்படி வாழாதவர்கள் தம்மைத் தாமே நொந்து கொள்ளாமல், தம்மை இகழ்ந்து பேசுபவர்களை நொந்து கொள்வதால் என்ன பயன்?
ai.explanation: This couplet explains that a person who does not live a life worthy of earning fame has only themselves to blame. The word 'tannōvār' (from 'tam' and 'nōvār') shows that such people fail to self-reflect or hold themselves accountable for their lack of reputation. Instead of correcting their own path, they get upset at others who mock or look down on them. The poet asks what possible use there is in blaming others when the root of the problem lies entirely within oneself.

words.gloss: to the people of the world

ai.literal: Blame, they say, to all the people of the world, if they do not obtain the legacy called fame.
ai.translation: For all people living on this earth, it is said to be a disgrace if they fail to acquire the lasting legacy called fame.
ai.modern: உலகில் வாழும் மக்கள் அனைவருக்கும், புகழ் என்று சொல்லப்படும் எஞ்சி நிற்கும் அழியாத செல்வத்தைப் பெறாவிட்டால், அதுவே பழி என்று கூறுவர்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the supreme importance of earning a good reputation during one's lifetime. The word 'icai' means fame, and 'eaccam' refers to a legacy or that which remains after one is gone. The poet states that if a person does not acquire this lasting legacy of fame, their life is considered a 'vacai', meaning a disgrace or blame. Thus, living a life that leaves no honorable memory behind is deemed a failure by the world.

ai.literal: The faultless bountiful yield will diminish of the land that bore the body without fame.
ai.translation: The rich, faultless yield of the earth will diminish if it must bear the burden of bodies that have achieved no fame.
ai.modern: புகழ் இல்லாத உடம்பைத் தாங்கிய நிலத்தின் குற்றமில்லாத வளமான விளைச்சல் குறைந்துபோகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the burden that people who live without earning fame place upon the earth. The poet states that the otherwise faultless and highly fertile land (வண்பயன்) will see its natural abundance diminish (குன்றும்) when it is forced to support the physical bodies (யாக்கை) of those who lack renown (இசையிலா). By linking the earth's fertility to the worthiness of its inhabitants, the verse poetically emphasizes that a life lived without leaving a good name is a drain on the world's resources.

words.gloss: are those who do not live

ai.literal: Blame being excluded, those who live indeed are those who live; fame being excluded, those who live indeed are those who do not live.
ai.translation: Those who live free from blame are the ones who truly live; those who live without earning fame are those who do not live at all.
ai.modern: பழி இல்லாமல் வாழ்பவர்களே உண்மையாக வாழ்பவர்கள்; புகழ் இல்லாமல் வாழ்பவர்கள் உயிரோடு இருந்தாலும் வாழாதவர்களே ஆவர்.
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts a meaningful life of honor with a meaningless existence. The poet defines true living through two conditions: the absence of blame (வசை) and the presence of fame (இசை). Those who live in such a way that they avoid reproach are celebrated as the truly living. On the other hand, those who exist without achieving any good reputation or fame are considered as good as dead, merely passing through life without truly living.
